description.sr:
Za proveru celog niza postoje dve metode. `every` vraća `true` ako funkcija koju joj damo vrati `true` za **svaki** element. `some` vraća `true` ako funkcija vrati `true` za **bar jedan** element. Na primer, `[2, 4].every((n) => n % 2 === 0)` je `true`, a `[1, 4].some((n) => n % 2 === 0)` je `true`.

Kod praznog niza nema nijednog elementa: `every` je tada uvek `true` (nema elementa koji bi pokvario uslov), a `some` je uvek `false` (nema elementa koji bi ga zadovoljio).

Napiši dve funkcije, `allPositive(nums)` i `anyNegative(nums)`. `nums` je niz brojeva.

- `allPositive` vraća `true` ako je svaki broj veći od `0`, inače `false`.
- `anyNegative` vraća `true` ako je bar jedan broj manji od `0`, inače `false`.

Pravila:
- `0` nije ni pozitivan ni negativan
- za prazan niz `allPositive` vraća `true`, a `anyNegative` vraća `false`

Primeri:
- `allPositive([1, 2, 3])` → `true`
- `allPositive([3, 0, 5])` → `false`, jer `0` nije pozitivan
- `allPositive([])` → `true`, jer nema broja koji bi pokvario uslov
- `anyNegative([5, -1, 2])` → `true`
- `anyNegative([0, 5])` → `false`, jer `0` nije negativan
- `anyNegative([])` → `false`, jer nema broja koji bi zadovoljio uslov
description.en:
There are two methods for checking a whole array. `every` returns `true` if the function we give it returns `true` for **every** element. `some` returns `true` if the function returns `true` for **at least one** element. For example, `[2, 4].every((n) => n % 2 === 0)` is `true`, and `[1, 4].some((n) => n % 2 === 0)` is `true`.

An empty array has no elements: `every` is then always `true` (there is no element that would break the condition), and `some` is always `false` (there is no element that would meet it).

Write two functions, `allPositive(nums)` and `anyNegative(nums)`. `nums` is an array of numbers.

- `allPositive` returns `true` if every number is greater than `0`, otherwise `false`.
- `anyNegative` returns `true` if at least one number is less than `0`, otherwise `false`.

Rules:
- `0` is neither positive nor negative
- for an empty array `allPositive` returns `true` and `anyNegative` returns `false`

Examples:
- `allPositive([1, 2, 3])` → `true`
- `allPositive([3, 0, 5])` → `false`, because `0` is not positive
- `allPositive([])` → `true`, because there is no number that would break the condition
- `anyNegative([5, -1, 2])` → `true`
- `anyNegative([0, 5])` → `false`, because `0` is not negative
- `anyNegative([])` → `false`, because there is no number that would meet the condition

text.sr:
Ovde pravimo (deklarišemo) funkciju. Funkcija je imenovan komad koda koji možemo da pozovemo koliko god puta hoćemo, svaki put sa drugim ulazom.

- `function allPositive` pravi funkciju sa tim imenom. Test je poziva baš tim imenom, pa mora biti napisano tačno ovako (velika i mala slova se razlikuju).
- `(nums)` je lista parametara. Parametar je prazno „mesto“ za ulaz: `nums` je niz brojeva. Poziv `allPositive([1, 2])` daje `nums = [1, 2]`.
- `{` otvara telo funkcije, a zatvara ga `}` u liniji 3.

Sama deklaracija ništa ne računa. Kod iz tela se izvršava tek kad funkciju pozovemo.
text.en:
Here we create (declare) a function. A function is a named piece of code that we can call as many times as we like, each time with different input.

- `function allPositive` creates a function with that name. The test calls it by exactly this name, so it must be spelled exactly like this (letter case matters).
- `(nums)` is the parameter list. A parameter is an empty “slot” for input: `nums` is an array of numbers. The call `allPositive([1, 2])` gives `nums = [1, 2]`.
- `{` opens the function body, and `}` on line 3 closes it.

The declaration itself computes nothing. The code in the body runs only when we call the function.

text.sr:
Proveravamo da li je svaki broj pozitivan.

- `nums.every(...)` vraća `true` samo ako uslov vrati `true` za svaki element. Čim naiđe na jedan za koji vrati `false`, staje i vraća `false`.
- `(n) => n > 0` je uslov. Strogo `> 0` jer `0` nije pozitivan.
- Za prazan niz nema nijednog elementa koji bi pokvario uslov, pa `every` vraća `true`. To je upravo ono što zadatak traži, bez posebnog slučaja.

```
[3, 0, 5]: 3 > 0 da, 0 > 0 ne → false (5 se ne proverava)
[]       : nema elemenata → true
```
text.en:
We check whether every number is positive.

- `nums.every(...)` returns `true` only if the condition returns `true` for every element. As soon as it meets one for which it returns `false`, it stops and returns `false`.
- `(n) => n > 0` is the condition. Strictly `> 0` because `0` is not positive.
- For an empty array there is no element that would break the condition, so `every` returns `true`. That is exactly what the task asks for, without a special case.

```
[3, 0, 5]: 3 > 0 yes, 0 > 0 no → false (5 is not checked)
[]       : no elements → true
```

Proveravamo da li je bar jedan broj negativan.

- `nums.some(...)` vraća `true` čim uslov vrati `true` za neki element. Ako nijedan ne zadovolji uslov, vraća `false`.
- `(n) => n < 0` je uslov. Strogo `< 0` jer `0` nije negativan.
- Za prazan niz nema nijednog elementa koji bi zadovoljio uslov, pa `some` vraća `false`.

```
[5, -1, 2]: 5 < 0 ne, -1 < 0 da → true (2 se ne proverava)
[0, 5]    : 0 < 0 ne, 5 < 0 ne → false
[]        : nema elemenata → false
```
text.en:
We check whether at least one number is negative.

- `nums.some(...)` returns `true` as soon as the condition returns `true` for some element. If none meets the condition, it returns `false`.
- `(n) => n < 0` is the condition. Strictly `< 0` because `0` is not negative.
- For an empty array there is no element that would meet the condition, so `some` returns `false`.

```
[5, -1, 2]: 5 < 0 no, -1 < 0 yes → true (2 is not checked)
[0, 5]    : 0 < 0 no, 5 < 0 no → false
[]        : no elements → false
```

text.sr:
Prolazimo kroz brojeve redom.

- `for (const n of nums)` znači: za svaki element niza `nums`, redom, uradi telo petlje. U svakom krugu `n` je jedan broj.
- `{` otvara telo petlje; zatvara ga `}` u liniji 4.
text.en:
We go through the numbers in order.

- `for (const n of nums)` means: for every element of the array `nums`, in order, run the loop body. In every round `n` is one number.
- `{` opens the loop body; it is closed by `}` on line 4.

text.sr:
Čim nađemo broj koji nije pozitivan, odgovor je `false`.

- `n <= 0` znači „manje ili jednako nuli“. Uključuje `0`, jer `0` nije pozitivan.
- `return false` odmah završava funkciju. Jedan loš broj je dovoljan, ostali se ne proveravaju.
- `if` bez vitičastih zagrada: u njega spada tačno jedna naredba posle uslova.

```
[3, 0, 5]
krug 1: n = 3 → 3 <= 0 ne
krug 2: n = 0 → 0 <= 0 da → return false
```
text.en:
As soon as we find a number that is not positive, the answer is `false`.

- `n <= 0` means “less than or equal to zero”. It includes `0`, because `0` is not positive.
- `return false` ends the function at once. One bad number is enough, the others are not checked.
- `if` without curly braces: exactly one statement after the condition belongs to it.

```
[3, 0, 5]
round 1: n = 3 → 3 <= 0 no
round 2: n = 0 → 0 <= 0 yes → return false
```

text.en: We reach this line only if no number broke the condition, because `return false` would already have stopped us. Then all are positive, so we return `true`. An empty array also arrives here, because the loop does not run even once, which is exactly what the task asks for.
